name: safe-dial
title: Safe Dial
description: A combination dial for a numeric code: turn it and let go, and the number goes into the next place of the code. The dial is UI SDK's slider over its numbers and the code is UI SDK's OTP input, so arrows, Enter, Backspace and typed digits all work, with enter(code) for agents.

[data-slot=\"safe-dial-stage\"].background-image: radial-gradient(ellipse 80% 60% at 50% 58%, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.07), transparent 70%), radial-gradient(circle at 1rem 1rem, #6d7379 0 3px, #2a2f33 3.5px 5px, transparent 5.5px), radial-gradient(circle at calc(100% - 1rem) 1rem, #6d7379 0 3px, #2a2f33 3.5px 5px, transparent 5.5px), radial-gradient(circle at 1rem calc(100% - 1rem), #6d7379 0 3px, #2a2f33 3.5px 5px, transparent 5.5px), radial-gradient(circle at calc(100% - 1rem) calc(100% - 1rem), #6d7379 0 3px, #2a2f33 3.5px 5px, transparent 5.5px), linear-gradient(160deg, #2b3034, #171a1d 70%)

[data-slot=\"safe-dial-steel\"].box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5), inset 0 2px 3px rgb(255 255 255 / 0.5), inset 0 -3px 6px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35)

[data-slot=\"safe-dial-knob\"].background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 50%, transparent 54%, rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35) 55%, transparent 58%), repeating-conic-gradient( from 0deg, rgb(0 0 0 / 0.28) 0 3deg, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.12) 3deg 10deg, transparent 10deg 15deg ), radial-gradient(circle at 40% 32%, #f1f3f5, #a7adb4 45%, #5d636a 100%)

docs: `<SafeDial label length numbers value|defaultValue onValueChange onComplete mask disabled name labels>`. `length` numbers (4 by default) on a dial of `numbers` (100 by default, 0 to 99), so each number takes two digits and the value is a string of digits like `"27046133"`. A drag turns the dial and releasing it enters the number under the index; arrows turn it a number (Shift ten) and wrap round, Enter enters it, Backspace takes the last number back and digits type straight into the code, which is UI SDK's OTPInput (paste and autofill work there too). `onComplete` runs when the code fills. `mask` shows dots; the input still holds the digits. An agent's `enter("27-04-61-33")` takes digits, numbers split by spaces or dashes, or an array, and fails with why on a wrong count or a number off the dial.
